name: VIPER
alternateName: Vision-language In Preclinical Evaluation of Rodents
description: VIPER is the first expert-curated benchmark for evaluating vision-language models on rodent toxicologic pathology. It contains 1,251 questions over 419 H&E-stained rat histology images spanning 9 organs (kidney, liver, thyroid, male reproductive system, urinary bladder, lung, heart, gastrointestinal tract, salivary gland) and three question formats (multiple-choice, KPrim, free-text). All questions were authored and validated by board-certified veterinary pathologists (ECVP).

citeAs: @inproceedings{weishaupt2026viper, title={VIPER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Vision-Language Models in Veterinary Pathology}, author={Weishaupt, Luca and de Brot, Simone and Asin, Javier and Grau-Roma, Lloren\c{c} and Reitsam, Nic and Song, Andrew H. and Bang, Dongmin and Le, Long Phi and Kather, Jakob Nikolas and Mahmood, Faisal and Jaume, Guillaume}, booktitle={Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems Datasets and Benchmarks}, year={2026}}
rai:dataCollection: Image regions of interest (ROIs) were extracted from two openly licensed preclinical-pathology resources: Open TG-GATEs (Japan NIBIO; CC BY-SA 2.1 JP; 157 studies) and the MMO atlas (Citlalli et al. 2022; CC BY-NC 4.0; 9 studies). For each organ, candidate ROIs were embedded with TRACE (Jaume et al. 2024) and K-means clustered into 20 bins per organ. A board-certified veterinary pathologist sampled across bins to span the morphologic range, then authored a seed question per ROI anchored in visible morphology. Seed questions were expanded into MCQ (5-option), KPrim (4-statement), and free-text variants by GPT-5.4. MCQ and KPrim variants were filtered for text-only guessability and regenerated if a no-image trial answered correctly. All questions were reviewed by a veterinary pathologist who manually approved, revised, or rejected each item.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each question was authored by VP1, the benchmark author and gold standard, an ECVP-board-certified veterinary pathologist. A reader study with VP1 plus two external ECVP-certified veterinary pathologists (VP2 and VP3) on a randomly sampled 100-question subset measured inter-rater agreement (Krippendorff's alpha reported in the paper).
rai:dataLimitations: VIPER is rat-only and rodent-pathology only; it does not capture neurotoxicity, the full species spectrum used in preclinical safety, or longitudinal/dose-response reasoning. Each instance is a single 1024x1024 ROI, not a slide-, organ-, or study-level sample, so VIPER does not characterize a full diagnostic system. Free-text scoring uses an LLM-as-judge with the rubric reported in the paper; the judge introduces unavoidable noise even when guided by structured rubrics. Question categories are unevenly populated (anatomy_identification has 362 questions; quantify_feature has 60). Source images are weighted toward MMO (1,062 questions) over TG-GATEs (189 questions) at the question level.
rai:dataBiases: All images are rat (Rattus norvegicus) tissue. The dataset inherits any cohort biases from its upstream sources (Open TG-GATEs and MMO), both of which are preclinical small-molecule toxicology study collections; therapeutic modalities outside small-molecule chemistry (e.g., biologics, gene therapy) are underrepresented. Pathologist authorship was concentrated in a single gold-standard author (VP1) for all 1,251 questions, with two external readers used only for reader-study validation on a 100-question subset. The 7-class question-category taxonomy is itself a curated lens; categories like 'identify_artifact' and 'quantify_feature' have small sample counts (63 and 60 respectively).
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses: evaluating vision-language models on rodent toxicologic pathology; probing visual grounding (does the model use the image?), domain transfer (does a human-pathology model work on rat tissue?), and robustness to MCQ option-order rotation; ablation studies that replace, blank, or randomize the image input to measure visual dependence. Out-of-scope uses: clinical decision-support benchmarks; slide-level, organ-level, or study-level diagnostic systems; species or organ systems not represented; longitudinal or dose-response reasoning.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive impact: VIPER lowers the barrier to evaluating pathology vision-language models in preclinical toxicology, a domain where progress has been constrained by the absence of public benchmarks. Better evaluations support more reliable models, and in turn more trustworthy decision-support tools for drug-safety assessment. Risks: model scores on VIPER must not be confused with clinical or regulatory readiness; high VIPER performance does not imply suitability for clinical decision-support. Misuse risk is low (the dataset contains no human or patient-identifying data and no proprietary information beyond the upstream public sources).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. The dataset contains no human-subject data, no patient identifiers, and no Protected Health Information (PHI). All images are H&E-stained rat tissue from publicly licensed preclinical toxicology resources (Open TG-GATEs and MMO).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Maintained by the Mahmood Lab at Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women's Hospital. Issues, errata, and questions are tracked at https://github.com/mahmoodlab/viper/issues. Versioned snapshots are released on the Hugging Face Hub; the published evaluation suite resolves a specific revision via the --dataset-revision flag.

prov:wasAttributedTo.prov:label: VIPER curation team (Mahmood Lab and academic collaborators)

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: ROI embedding and clustering
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Candidate ROIs per organ were embedded with the TRACE vision encoder (Jaume et al. 2024) and K-means clustered into 20 bins per organ. The pathologist sampled across bins to span the morphologic range.

prov:wasAttributedTo.prov:label: TRACE vision encoder (Jaume et al. 2024)
prov:wasAttributedTo.sc:description: Self-supervised pathology foundation model trained on TG-GATEs. Used here only to compute ROI embeddings; no fine-tuning.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Seed question authoring by gold-standard veterinary pathologist (VP1)
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: For each selected ROI, VP1 — the benchmark author and gold standard — wrote one seed question answerable from the visible morphology. 708 seed questions were initially authored; 247 were dropped during downstream filtering, leaving 419 seeds that expanded into 1,251 final question-format variants.

prov:wasAttributedTo.prov:label: VP1 (gold-standard author; identity anonymized)
prov:wasAttributedTo.sc:description: ECVP-board-certified veterinary pathologist; gold-standard author of all 1,251 questions.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Synthetic question-format expansion (MCQ / KPrim / free-text) by GPT-5.4
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Each VP1 seed question was expanded by GPT-5.4 into three formats: MCQ (5 options), KPrim (4 true/false statements), and free-text. Each free-text variant was paired with an LLM-generated scoring rubric. The LLM was given the seed question and reference answer; no images were sent. All expansions were approved or revised by VP1.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Text-only guessability filtering
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Each MCQ and KPrim candidate was queried against GPT-5.2 (temperature 0) with the stem and options but no image: three trials per MCQ with cyclic-shifted option order, one trial per KPrim. A candidate was flagged if any MCQ trial answered correctly (strict policy) or if the worst-case KPrim trial answered ≥3/4 statements correctly. Flagged candidates were regenerated by GPT-5.4 before escalation to VP1. Free-text variants were not filtered.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Final manual approval by gold-standard veterinary pathologist (VP1)
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: All 1,251 final questions, choices, and rubrics were reviewed and either approved, revised, or rejected by VP1.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: External reader study (Krippendorff inter-rater agreement)
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: 100 question-image pairs (Set A) were sampled and independently answered by VP1, VP2, and VP3 through a custom online platform; inter-rater agreement was quantified with Krippendorff alpha. A second 100-question Set B expanded the study to a board-certified physician pathologist (PP1) and to a no-image condition. Results are reported in the paper and appendix.

prov:wasAttributedTo.prov:label: VP2 (independent external reader; identity anonymized)
prov:wasAttributedTo.sc:description: ECVP-board-certified veterinary pathologist. VP2 and VP3 are drawn from a pool spanning COMPATH (University of Bern) and UC Davis.

prov:wasAttributedTo.prov:label: PP1 (physician-pathologist reader; identity anonymized)
prov:wasAttributedTo.sc:description: Board-certified physician pathologist trained in human pathology, at a Mass General Brigham / Harvard Medical School–affiliated US institution.

distribution.name: viper.parquet
distribution.description: All 1,251 VIPER questions with their associated H&E ROIs, choices, gold-standard answers, scoring rubrics, and per-question metadata (organ, category, magnification, source).

recordSet.name: questions
recordSet.description: One row per VIPER question (1,251 total).

field.name: image
field.description: 1024x1024 RGB H&E-stained rat histology ROI, PNG-encoded.

field.name: image_id
field.description: Stable content-hashed identifier of the form viper_<organ_slug>_<sha256(image_bytes)[:12]>.

field.name: question_type
field.description: Question format. One of: mcq (multiple-choice, 5 options), kprim (4 true/false statements), free_text (open-ended).

field.name: answer
field.description: Gold-standard answer. MCQ: option letter (A-E). KPrim: JSON-encoded list of four booleans. Free-text: reference answer string.

field.name: choices
field.description: Answer options. Five strings for MCQ, four statements for KPrim, empty list for free-text.

field.name: synonyms
field.description: Optional JSON-encoded list of acceptable free-text synonyms used during LLM-as-judge scoring.

field.name: scoring_rubric
field.description: Optional free-text grading rubric provided to the LLM judge for free-text scoring.

field.name: organ
field.description: Paper-aligned organ label. One of: kidney, liver, thyroid, male_reproductive_system, urinary_bladder, lung, heart, gastrointestinal_tract, salivary_gland.

field.name: category
field.description: Paper §2 question-category taxonomy. One of: identify_anatomy, probe_over_reading, localize_in_image, identify_pathology, characterize_feature, identify_artifact, quantify_feature.

field.name: source
field.description: Upstream image source. One of: TG-GATEs (CC BY-SA 2.1 JP), MMO (CC BY-NC 4.0).
